title: Converting a private company into a Section 8 company
law: Sections 8, 12, 13, 14, 15, 96, 100, 117 and 173; Rules 19 and 20 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014 (as amended in 2023); Rule 24 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014; Secretarial Standards 1 and 2
summary: Turns an existing private company into a not-for-profit Section 8 company, with a licence from the Registrar and a new name without the word Private Limited.
when: When the members want to run the company only for charitable or similar objects and plough all profits back into those objects.
applies: Private company (registered under the 2013 Act or earlier law)

steps.d: The promoters apply to the Registrar of the state where the company will sit, using the RUN service, and pay the prescribed fee.
The board approves the conversion, the altered MOA and AOA, the draft notice of the general meeting, and authorises a director or the company secretary to handle filings.
steps.time: Notice: 7 days, or shorter if directors agree

steps.t: Pass a special resolution at a general meeting
steps.d: Members approve the conversion and the alteration of the MOA and AOA to match Section 8 norms. Send notice with an explanatory statement. Shorter notice needs consent of members as the law allows.
File the special resolution with the Registrar, with the usual attachments and fee.
steps.time: Within 30 days of passing the resolution

steps.d: Apply on INC-12 with fee. The company will not use Limited or Private Limited in its name. Attach the documents listed in the checklist, including the professional's declaration on INC-14 and the company's own declaration on INC-15.
docs: Estimated income and expenditure for 3 years

steps.d: At its own cost, publish the notice at least once in a local-language newspaper and an English newspaper circulating in the district of the registered office, and on the websites the Central Government notifies. Send a copy of the notice to the Registrar at once.
steps.time: Within one week of the application
forms: INC-26 (as named in the reference note)

steps.d: The Registrar looks at the last two years' financial statements (or one year, if that is all there is, with board and audit reports). The Registrar considers objections received within 30 days of publication and may consult other authorities. If satisfied, a licence is issued. The Registrar may require extra conditions in the MOA or AOA.

Update every copy of the MOA and AOA. Display the new MOA, AOA and certificate of incorporation at every office. Engrave the name on the seal. Print the required details on official papers and on bills of exchange, promissory notes and similar instruments. Tell banks, authorities and service providers.
Update PAN, GST, shops and establishment, factories, inter-state migrant workmen, private security agencies, EPF and ESIC, other labour laws and any industry-specific registrations.

forms.purpose: Public notice (as named in the reference note)
Licence (as named in the reference note)
Licence (as named in the reference note)

checklist: Altered AOA (and entrenched AOA, if any)
Notice and explanatory statement of general meeting
INC-14 from CA, CS, CMA or advocate
Statement of assets and liabilities (current or within 30 days)
List of promoters, directors and KMP
Estimated income and expenditure for 3 years
Newspaper notices and copy sent to Registrar

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve conversion to a Section 8 company
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

meetings.title: General meeting to approve conversion and new constitution
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter if members consent as the law allows)

resolutions.title: Approval of conversion and calling of general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, subject to approval of members and the Registrar's licence under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, the conversion of {co} into a company under Section 8, with the new name [proposed name], be and is hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the altered Memorandum and Articles of Association placed before the meeting be approved for submission to members. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the draft notice of the general meeting to be held on [date] be approved and [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to issue it and to file all forms, applications and documents with the Registrar and other authorities.

resolutions.title: Conversion into Section 8 company and alteration of MOA
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Sections 8, 13 and 14 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rules 19 and 20 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, and subject to the licence of the Registrar, the consent of members be and is hereby given to convert {co} into a company under Section 8, to change its name to [proposed name], and to alter the Memorandum of Association as set out in the draft placed before the meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to make all applications and filings and to accept any change the Registrar requires.
resolutions.explanatory: The company wishes to carry on [objects, e.g. promoting education or charity], apply its profits only towards those objects and pay no dividend to members. For this it must adopt Section 8 objects and a name without the words Private Limited. The draft MOA and AOA are open for inspection at the registered office during business hours. No director or manager is interested in this item except as a member. The board recommends the special resolution.

resolutions.title: Adoption of new Articles of Association
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 14 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the Articles of Association of {co} be altered by adopting the new Articles placed before the meeting, in substitution for the existing Articles, to conform to Section 8. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a copy of this resolution be filed in Form MGT-14 within 30 days.
resolutions.explanatory: The existing Articles must be replaced so that they match the not-for-profit features of Section 8. The new Articles are available for inspection at the registered office. The board recommends the special resolution.

docs.title: Newspaper notice (text)
paras: Notice is given that {co}, having its registered office at [address], has applied to the Registrar of Companies, [city], to convert into a company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, with the name [proposed name], and to alter its Memorandum of Association accordingly.

Any person whose interest may be affected may send written objections to the Registrar of Companies, [office address], within 30 days of this notice, with a copy to the company at its registered office.
By order of the Board. [Name], Director. Date: [date].

docs.title: Declaration letter outline for the professional
paras: I, [name], [CA/CS/CMA/Advocate], membership no. [number], have examined the MOA, AOA and papers of {co} and confirm that they comply with Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the rules.

flags: The reference note names INC-26 for the notice. INC-26 is normally the notice for shifting the registered office; for Section 8 licence/conversion I believe the Rule 19/20 notice is a different form (INC-19). Verify the current form on the MCA portal.
The reference note mixes 'Board or General Meeting' in step 2. A special resolution of members is needed (Section 14), so hold a board meeting first and then a general meeting.

The reference note says licence in INC-16 or INC-17. Confirm which applies after the 2023 amendment rules; also check whether the current rules route private-to-Section 8 conversion through a different application form.
The post-conversion step about informing parties of a 'new registered office' looks like a stray point; the office changes only if it is actually being shifted.
MGT-14 deadline of 30 days is as per Section 117; check whether the reference note's reference to the SS-1 and SS-2 dates fits your meeting plan.

title: Appointing an internal auditor
law: Section 138; Rule 13 of Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014; Sections 117, 144, 173, 179 and 450; Rule 8 of Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014; Rule 24 of Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014; Secretarial Standard 1; SEBI LODR (for listed entities)
summary: Check whether the company must have an internal auditor, choose an eligible person, appoint by board resolution and set how the audit is done and reported.
when: When the company falls in a class that must have an internal audit, or chooses to have one.
applies: Listed companies, unlisted public companies and private companies that cross the limits in step 1

steps.t: Check if internal audit is required
steps.d: Listed companies must always have it. Unlisted public companies need it if, in the previous financial year, paid-up capital was Rs. 50 crore or more, or turnover Rs. 200 crore or more, or outstanding loans from banks or public financial institutions exceeded Rs. 100 crore at any time, or deposits were Rs. 25 crore or more at any time. Private companies need it if turnover was Rs. 200 crore or more, or such loans exceeded Rs. 100 crore at any time.

A chartered accountant or cost accountant (in practice or not), or another professional the board decides on. It can be an individual, a firm or a body corporate, and an employee or an outsider. A company secretary may also do internal audit.
The statutory auditor appointed under Section 139 cannot do internal audit for the company, its holding company or its subsidiary, directly or indirectly.
Check eligibility and get a written letter from the person confirming eligibility and willingness to act.
Give 7 days' notice, or use shorter notice with the directors' consent. Follow SS-1. Appoint the internal auditor by a resolution passed at the meeting, as Rule 8 requires.

steps.t: Prepare certified copy and file MGT-14
steps.d: Make a certified true copy of the resolution. Where required, file MGT-14 under Sections 117 and 179.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the board meeting

steps.d: Send the auditor a letter setting out duties, pay, terms of engagement and other details.

steps.t: Fix scope and manner of audit
steps.d: The audit committee (if the company must have one under Section 177), otherwise the board, decides the scope, working method, frequency and methodology in consultation with the internal auditor.

The auditor reports to the audit committee or board at the agreed intervals. The report covers scope, objectives, method, findings, conclusions and recommendations and flags major issues, risks or frauds. The committee or board acts on findings and tracks follow-up. The auditor also shares results and information with the statutory auditor.
steps.time: As decided by the committee or board

steps.d: The audit committee must review the appointment, removal and pay of the chief internal auditor, internal audit reports on control weaknesses, auditor performance, adequacy of controls, structure, staffing and seniority of the department, coverage and frequency. Serious findings on suspected fraud or material control failure go to the board.

forms.deadline: Within 30 days of the board meeting (not needed for private companies, see flags)

checklist: Applicability test done for last financial year
Not the statutory auditor of the company or its group
Board resolution passed at a meeting
Scope and frequency of audit fixed
Audit committee or board review dates planned

meetings.title: Board meeting to appoint the internal auditor
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

resolutions.title: Appointment of internal auditor
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 13 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, [name of auditor], [Chartered Accountant / Cost Accountant / other professional] (membership no. [number]), who has given a written consent and is not disqualified under Section 144, be and is hereby appointed as Internal Auditor of {co} for the financial year [year] on a remuneration of Rs. [amount] and on the terms in the appointment letter. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to issue the appointment letter and to file Form MGT-14, if required.

docs.title: Consent letter from proposed internal auditor
paras: To the Board of Directors, {co}.

I, [name], [qualification], confirm that I am eligible for appointment as Internal Auditor under Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013, that I am not the statutory auditor of the company, its holding company or any subsidiary, and that I am willing to act. Date: [date]. Signed: [name].

docs.title: Appointment letter
paras: Dear [name], the Board of {co} has appointed you as Internal Auditor from [date] under Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Your scope of work is [scope]. You will report to the [Audit Committee / Board] at [frequency]. Your fee is Rs. [amount]. Other terms: [terms].
Please sign and return a copy to confirm acceptance. For {co}, [name of director]. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note cites the SEBI LODR Regulations as 2014 in the law list and 2015 later. The correct year is 2015.

The reference note says MGT-14 is needed within 30 days. Private companies are exempt from Section 117(3)(g) by the MCA notification of 5 June 2015 as per the reference note; confirm the current position for unlisted public companies.
Table in the reference note is scrambled. I read it as the Rule 13 limits; check against the current rule before relying on the thresholds.
The reference note list of persons includes 'such other professional as the Board decides'; check the exact wording of Rule 13 for any ICSI or other body recognition.
private: A private company is exempt from Section 117(3)(g) under the MCA notification of 5 June 2015, so it need not file Form MGT-14 for Board resolutions. The Listing Regulations do not apply to unlisted public companies or private companies.

title: Appointing a woman director
law: Second proviso to Section 149(1); Rule 3 of Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014; Sections 161, 178 and 184
summary: Steps to appoint at least one woman director when the company's class requires it: board appointment as additional director, then confirmation by members.
when: When the company is listed, or is a public company over the size limits and has no woman on its board.
applies: Every listed company; other public companies with paid-up capital of Rs. 100 crore or more, or turnover of Rs. 300 crore or more

steps.d: If the company has a Nomination and Remuneration Committee under Section 178, it recommends the appointment, terms and pay to the board.
The proposed woman director gives her consent to act and sends an intimation that she is not disqualified.
She must hold a valid DIN and digital signature certificate before appointment. If she has no DIN, apply first.
Check eligibility and conflict of interest under Section 184 and collect the disclosure of interest.
Pass the resolution to appoint her as additional director, subject to approval of members at the general meeting.
Disclose the decision to the exchange within 30 minutes from the close of the board meeting.
File the return of appointment with the Registrar, with the board resolution, the consent and the declaration about disqualification.
At the next AGM, pass an ordinary resolution to confirm her as a director.
Disclose the general meeting proceedings to the stock exchange within 48 hours of the meeting and post them on the website within two working days.
File again to show the change of designation from additional director to director.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the general meeting

steps.d: Enter her details in the register of directors and key managerial personnel and in the register of contracts or arrangements in which directors are interested (MBP-4).

forms.purpose: Return of appointment, and again for change of designation
Register of contracts in which directors are interested (entry)

checklist: Company meets the class test in Rule 3

meetings.title: Board meeting to appoint the woman director
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

meetings.title: General meeting to confirm the woman director

resolutions.title: Appointment of woman director as additional director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Sections 149, 152 and 161 of the Companies Act, 2013, Rule 3 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014, the Articles of Association and on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Ms. [name] (DIN [number]) be and is hereby appointed as an Additional Director (woman director) of {co} with effect from [date], to hold office up to the date of the next annual general meeting, subject to approval of members. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to file Form DIR-12 and make all stock exchange disclosures.

resolutions.title: Confirmation of appointment of woman director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Sections 149, 152 and 161 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Articles of Association, Ms. [name] (DIN [number]), who was appointed as an Additional Director on [date] and holds office up to this meeting, and who has consented to act and is not disqualified, be and is hereby appointed as a Director of {co}, liable to retire by rotation [or: not liable to retire by rotation].
resolutions.explanatory: Ms. [name] was appointed as additional director on [date] to meet the requirement of at least one woman director under Section 149(1). Her brief profile: [profile]. She has given consent in DIR-2 and a declaration of non-disqualification. Notice under Section 160 [if required] has been received. No director other than Ms. [name] is interested in the resolution. The board recommends the ordinary resolution.

docs.title: Consent letter outline
paras: I, [name], DIN [number], consent to act as director of {co} and confirm I am not disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note says to disclose general meeting proceedings 'before 48 hours' of the meeting end. This reads wrong; the listing rules allow up to 48 hours (outcome) and voting results within 2 working days. Check the current LODR.

For listed companies, I believe shareholder approval for an additional director must be obtained within three months from appointment or at the next general meeting, whichever is earlier. The reference note only mentions the next AGM.
The Act also needs an intermittent woman-director vacancy to be filled within three months or the next board meeting, whichever is later. Not in the reference note.
The reference note mentions DIR-3 for DIN; DIN for new applicants now usually goes through SPICe+ or the current MCA route. Verify.
Listed companies must also meet LODR rules on an independent woman director; not covered in the reference note.
private: A woman director is not required in a private company, unless it is a subsidiary of a public company that meets the size tests.

title: Re-appointing an independent director for a second term
law: Section 149; Rules 4, 5 and 6 of Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014; Schedule IV (Part V); Sections 101, 102, 108, 110, 134, 164, 165, 170, 173, 178; Rule 20 of Management and Administration Rules, 2014
summary: How to check, evaluate and re-appoint an independent director for a second term of up to five years by special resolution.
when: When the first term of an independent director (up to five years) is ending and the board wants to continue with them.
applies: Companies that must have independent directors (listed public companies and larger public companies)

steps.d: Check the company is active on the MCA master data, and the CIN, date and type match. Read the MOA and AOA: make sure they do not block re-appointment or set special conditions for independent directors.

Confirm no disqualification under Section 164, valid DIN, qualification under Rule 5, registration in the independent directors' databank (IICA, Rule 6), directorship count within Section 165(1), no link to promoters or directors (Section 149(12)) and no pecuniary relationship beyond limits (Section 149(6)). Get the declaration of compliance with Rule 6(1) and (2).

Confirm the first term is complete (up to 5 years), the person will serve no more than two consecutive terms and no three-year cooling-off period is running. During cooling-off, the person cannot be linked to the company in any capacity.
Get consent to act, the declaration of independence under Section 149(7) and the disclosure of interest.

The whole board, without the director being evaluated, assesses participation, independence of judgment, awareness of the business and risks, ethics and conflict handling, and leadership for chairs. The report decides whether to extend the term.
Where an NRC is required, it reviews the documents and the evaluation and, if satisfied, recommends a second term of not more than five years, with reasons.
Under Section 173 and SS-1, the board considers the NRC recommendation, approves re-appointment subject to members, approves the notice of the general meeting and authorises issue and filings.

Send notice to members, directors and auditors with an explanatory statement covering the reasons for re-appointment, evaluation summary, NRC and board recommendation and confirmation of independence. Provide e-voting where required.
steps.time: At least 21 clear days; e-voting open 3 days, closing the day before the meeting

steps.d: Hold the meeting under Sections 96 or 100 and SS-2. Pass a special resolution (75% of votes cast in favour). Where e-voting is used, appoint a scrutinizer and get the report.
Right after the resolution, send the letter with terms, duties and pay.
File with the certified resolution, notice and explanatory statement, any shorter notice consents, minutes extract and other attachments.
File the return with the certified special resolution, consent and declaration of independence.

Update the register of directors and KMP (Section 170) and the register of contracts (MBP-4). Disclose the re-appointment in the Board's report under Section 134, saying it followed the performance evaluation.

checklist: E-voting arranged and scrutinizer appointed (if needed)

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve re-appointment and call the general meeting
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

meetings.title: General meeting to re-appoint the independent director
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter only with consent of the required majority)

resolutions.title: Re-appointment of independent director, subject to members
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Sections 149 and 152 and Schedule IV of the Companies Act, 2013 and on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and after considering the performance evaluation report, re-appointment of [name] (DIN [number]) as an Independent Director of {co} for a second term of [number] years from [date] to [date] be and is hereby approved, subject to approval of members by special resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the draft notice of the general meeting to be held on [date] be approved and [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to issue it and make all filings.

resolutions.title: Re-appointment of independent director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Sections 149(10), 149(11) and 152 and Schedule IV of the Companies Act, 2013, [name] (DIN [number]), who has given the declaration of independence and consent, and whose first term ends on [date], be and is hereby re-appointed as an Independent Director of {co}, not liable to retire by rotation, for a second term of [number] years from [date] to [date].
resolutions.explanatory: [Name], aged [age], joined the board on [date]. The board, on the NRC's recommendation and based on the performance evaluation, considers that [his/her] skills and contribution benefit the company. [He/She] has declared that [he/she] meets the independence criteria in Section 149(6), is registered in the databank and is not disqualified. The terms of appointment are open for inspection at the registered office. No director other than [name] is interested. The board recommends the special resolution.

docs.title: NRC recommendation
paras: Meeting of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee of {co} held on [date]. The committee reviewed the eligibility documents, declaration of independence and the performance evaluation report of [name] (DIN [number]).

The committee finds that [he/she] has met the criteria of independence and performed satisfactorily, based on [grounds]. The committee recommends to the board the re-appointment of [name] for a second term of [number] years.

docs.title: Appointment letter
paras: Dear [name], following approval by members on [date], you are re-appointed as Independent Director of {co} for a term of [number] years from [date].
Your duties, code of conduct, committee roles, sitting fees of Rs. [amount] and other terms: [terms]. Please confirm acceptance by signing a copy. For {co}, [name of director]. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note says e-voting is for companies with 1,000 or more members and that private companies are exempt from Rule 20. Rule 20 covers listed companies and companies with 1,000 or more members; I believe a private company with 1,000+ members is not exempt. Verify.

The reference note says private companies need not appoint independent directors and that Section 149(4) applies to public companies with paid-up capital of Rs. 10 crore or turnover Rs. 100 crore 'etc.'. I believe the test also includes outstanding loans, debentures and deposits above Rs. 50 crore. Verify.
The 75% test applies to votes cast, not to all members.
For listed companies, check LODR conditions on shareholder approval of independent directors in addition to the Act.

items: The rule covers listed public companies and certain public companies, for example those with paid-up capital of Rs. 10 crore or more or turnover of Rs. 100 crore or more.
Private companies need none, though they may appoint one voluntarily.
Section 178(1) does not require one for a private company, so the committee's recommendation step is skipped unless the company set one up voluntarily.
Rule 20 of the Management and Administration Rules exempts private companies from providing e-voting.
Schedule IV's evaluation of independent directors is not strictly binding on private companies. It is good practice, not a legal duty, for them.

title: Handling a director's resignation (unlisted public company)
law: Section 168 read with Rules 15 and 16 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014; Sections 134(3)(q), 170(1) and 173
summary: Records a director's resignation, files the notice with the Registrar and updates the company's records and disclosures.
applies: Unlisted public company (private company differences noted)

steps.d: The director gives a signed and dated letter stating when the resignation takes effect. Email or hard copy is fine.
Any director signs and dates the letter with the company stamp, or acknowledges it electronically.
Call a board meeting under Section 173 and SS-1, with at least 7 days' notice or shorter notice where permitted.
The board notes the resignation by resolution.

File with the Registrar. The resignation takes effect from the date the company receives the letter or the date the director names, whichever is later. Attach the certified resolution, the resignation letter and, optionally, proof of acknowledgment.
steps.time: Within 30 days from receipt of the resignation notice

steps.d: The resigning director may also inform the Registrar directly.

Give details of directors and KMP who resigned or were appointed in the Board's report (Section 134(3)(q)), report it in the annual return of that financial year, and post it on the website, if there is one.
Update the register of directors and KMP under Section 170(1).

forms.purpose: Notice of resignation filed by the company
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of receipt of the notice

forms.purpose: Optional notice by the resigning director

checklist: Board report and annual return updated
Register of directors and KMP updated

meetings.title: Board meeting to note the resignation

resolutions.title: Noting the resignation of a director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the resignation letter dated [date] of Mr./Ms. [name] (DIN [number]) from the office of Director of {co}, received on [date] and effective from [effective date], be and is hereby taken on record under Section 168 of the Companies Act, 2013. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board places on record its appreciation of the services rendered. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to file Form DIR-12 and to update the registers.

docs.title: Resignation letter
paras: To the Board of Directors, {co}. I, [name], DIN [number], resign from the office of Director of the company with effect from [date]. The reason is [reason]. Please file the necessary forms. Date: [date]. Signed: [name].

flags: The reference note counts the DIR-12 period from receipt of the notice. Rule 17 normally counts 30 days from the date of the change, which is the effective date. If the director names a later date, count from that date. Verify.

The reference note does not mention that a private company need not hold a board meeting unless its Articles say so; an acknowledged letter can then be the attachment to DIR-12 (per the reference note note).
private: A private company need not hold a Board meeting for this unless its Articles require one. The resignation letter, acknowledged with a date and the company stamp, is a valid attachment to Form DIR-12 as proof of cessation.

title: Removing a director by the members
law: Sections 169 and 115; Rule 23 of Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014; Sections 101, 102, 163, 242
summary: Members remove a director before the end of the term by an ordinary resolution passed after special notice, with the director given a right to be heard.
when: When members holding enough shares want to remove a director.
applies: All companies (private companies also, subject to the Articles)

steps.t: Check the director can be removed
steps.d: The director must not be one appointed by the Tribunal under Section 242, or appointed by proportional representation under Section 163.
Make sure nothing in the Articles changes or limits the statutory removal process, for example special rights for nominee directors or investors.

Members give written special notice under Section 115 and Rule 23(1). They must hold at least 1% of total voting power or shares with at least Rs. 5,00,000 paid up, alone or together, on the date of notice. The notice is given not earlier than 3 months, and at least 14 clear days, before the meeting.
steps.time: 14 clear days before the meeting, at most 3 months before

steps.t: Send a copy to the director
steps.d: The company sends the notice to the director at once. The director may speak at the meeting, whether or not a member.

The director may send a written representation and ask that it be sent to members. The company mentions it in the notice and sends copies. If there is no time or the company fails, the director can ask for it to be read at the meeting, in addition to speaking. The Tribunal can stop circulation if the representation is abusive and may order the director to pay costs.

The board notes the special notice and approves calling the general meeting and its notice, including the date, time, place, text of the ordinary resolution, any representation and the explanatory statement.

Send notice to all members. The notice must state the resolution is moved under Section 169 and attach any representation. If notice cannot reach all in the usual way, advertise it in an English paper and a vernacular paper of wide circulation in the state, and on the website. Pass an ordinary resolution by simple majority of those present and voting.
steps.time: Reference note: at least 7 clear days (see flags)

steps.d: File electronically with fee. Attach the certified resolution, notice of the meeting and proof of dispatch of the special notice, where applicable.
docs: Proof of dispatch of special notice

steps.d: A new director may be appointed at the same meeting, but only if special notice of that appointment was given as required by Section 169. If not filled, it is a casual vacancy that the board or members can fill under the Act and Articles. The new director holds office only for the rest of the removed director's term.

checklist: Director is not Tribunal-appointed or proportional-representation director
Special notice signed by members meeting 1% or Rs. 5 lakh test
Notice received within 3 months and at least 14 clear days before meeting

meetings.title: Board meeting to call the general meeting on removal
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

meetings.title: General meeting to remove the director
meetings.notice_days: See flags (the reference note says 7 clear days)

resolutions.title: Noting special notice and calling general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the special notice dated [date] received under Section 115 of the Companies Act, 2013 from members holding [percentage/amount] of the voting power or paid-up capital of {co}, proposing removal of Mr./Ms. [name] (DIN [number]) as Director under Section 169, be noted. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] and the draft notice with the explanatory statement, and any written representation of the director, be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to send them to all members, the director and the auditors.

resolutions.title: Removal of a director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 169 of the Companies Act, 2013 and on the special notice received from members, Mr./Ms. [name] (DIN [number]) be and is hereby removed from the office of Director of {co} with effect from [date]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to file Form DIR-12 and do all things needed.
resolutions.explanatory: Special notice has been received from members proposing the removal of Mr./Ms. [name]. The director was given a copy and the chance to make a representation. [The director's representation, if any, is attached.] Reason stated by the members: [reason].

docs.title: Special notice by members (outline)
paras: To the Board of Directors, {co}. We, the undersigned members holding [number] shares / [percentage] of voting power, give special notice under Section 115 of the Companies Act, 2013 of our intention to move at the general meeting to be held on [date] an ordinary resolution to remove Mr./Ms. [name] (DIN [number]) as director under Section 169. Signed: [names and folio numbers]. Date: [date].

docs.title: Newspaper notice (text)
paras: Notice is given that a general meeting of {co} will be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] to consider an ordinary resolution under Section 169 of the Companies Act, 2013 for removal of Mr./Ms. [name] as Director. The director has [made / not made] a written representation. Copies are available at the registered office. By order of the Board. [Name], Company Secretary. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note says the general meeting notice need only be 7 clear days. Section 101 requires 21 clear days for any general meeting, unless members holding 95% (as the law and Articles allow) agree to shorter notice. Verify before relying on 7 days.
The reference note cites Section 169(2) for special notice of the new appointment; check the exact sub-section.
The reference note refers to 'Extra-Ordinary General Meeting' for removal; it can also be moved at an AGM.

title: Removing a director under Section 169 (public and listed company view)
law: Section 169 and applicable rules; Sections 14, 110, 173; Rule 22 of Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014; SEBI LODR (for listed companies)
summary: A checklist-style route to remove a director, with the extra points for NRC, stock exchange intimation and postal ballot for listed and large companies.
when: When members serve special notice to remove a director, or to appoint someone in place of a director removed.
applies: Public and listed companies (private differences noted in flags)

steps.d: Confirm the company has received special notice from members holding at least 1% of voting power or shares with at least Rs. 5,00,000 paid up on the date of notice, for the removal, or for appointing someone in the removed director's place.
See whether the Articles restrict removal. If they do, alter them first under Section 14.

Section 169 does not apply to Tribunal-appointed directors (Section 242), proportional representation directors (Section 163) and, as the reference note says, independent directors re-appointed under Section 149(10).
If an NRC exists, get its recommendation under the criteria and policy it follows.
Give notice under Section 173 and SS-1. Approve the removal proposal and call an EGM or include the item in the AGM notice.
Listed companies report the board meeting outcome to the exchange.
Send the notice to all members and advertise it in a vernacular and an English newspaper.

steps.t: Send special notice to the director
steps.d: Give the director a copy of the special notice and allow a written representation.
The company must send the director's written representation to members. The director may ask for it to be read at the meeting.

steps.t: Hold the general meeting or postal ballot
steps.d: Hold the meeting under Section 96 or 100 and SS-2 and pass an ordinary resolution by simple majority. The reference note also names postal ballot for listed companies or companies with more than 200 members. The director must be heard before the vote.
Listed companies inform the exchange of the result of the meeting or postal ballot.
File with the Registrar.

checklist: Special notice meets 1% or Rs. 5 lakh test

meetings.title: Board meeting on removal of a director
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

meetings.title: General meeting to remove the director

resolutions.title: Calling general meeting on removal of director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the special notice dated [date] received from members of {co} proposing removal of Mr./Ms. [name] (DIN [number]) as Director under Section 169 of the Companies Act, 2013 be noted, and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee's recommendation, if any, be taken on record. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a general meeting be held on [date] at [time] and the draft notice be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to issue the notice, advertise it and inform the stock exchanges.

resolutions.title: Removal of director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 169 of the Companies Act, 2013, Mr./Ms. [name] (DIN [number]) be and is hereby removed from the office of Director of {co} with effect from [date]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to file Form DIR-12 and make all stock exchange disclosures.
resolutions.explanatory: Members holding [percentage] of voting power have given special notice for the removal of Mr./Ms. [name]. The director has been given a copy and the chance to be heard and to make a representation. The board recommends [or: makes no recommendation on] the resolution.

docs.title: Notice to concerned director
paras: Dear [name], {co} has received the attached special notice dated [date] proposing your removal as director under Section 169 of the Companies Act, 2013 at the general meeting on [date].

You may make a written representation and ask that it be circulated to members, and you may be heard at the meeting. Please send any representation by [date]. For {co}, [name], Company Secretary. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note suggests postal ballot as an alternative. I believe Rule 22 bars postal ballot for business where a director or auditor has a right to be heard at the meeting, which covers removal under Section 169. Also the cited Section 110(1)(b)(iv) looks wrong. Verify.
The reference note lists independent directors re-appointed under Section 149(10) as outside Section 169. This is not in Section 169 as I know it; verify.
NRC recommendation on removal is not required by Section 169; it is a governance step for companies with an NRC.
The reference note gives no notice period for the general meeting; Section 101 needs 21 clear days unless shorter notice is validly agreed, and Section 115 needs 14 clear days for the special notice.
private: A private company need not take the Nomination and Remuneration Committee's recommendation, postal ballot does not apply to it, and there is no stock exchange intimation of the Board or general meeting outcome.

title: Holding a physical board meeting, passing resolutions and recording minutes
law: Section 173; Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014; Secretarial Standard 1
summary: Step-by-step guide from fixing the date and sending notice, through conducting the meeting, to circulating and signing the minutes.
when: Whenever the board needs to meet in person to take decisions.
applies: All companies except one person companies with a single director; small companies have a lighter frequency rule

steps.t: Fix the date, agenda and notice
steps.d: Choose a date not more than 120 days after the previous board meeting. Decide the agenda and prepare the notice.
Send to all directors and invitees, by post or electronically, seven days before the meeting.
Send the notes to agenda, annexures and draft resolutions with the notice or separately.
Arrange travel for outstation directors and invitees. If anyone will join by video or other audio-visual means, arrange the equipment.
If the company has no chairman, the directors elect one for the meeting.
The chairman, with the company secretary, checks quorum. Once present, the chairman declares the meeting in order and follows the agenda.

steps.t: Take items for noting, then discuss
steps.d: Place items for noting first, then the items that need a resolution, for discussion.

After discussion, the chairman or company secretary puts the resolution to vote. Directors for and against cast votes. It passes if it gets the needed majority. Record discussion, assent and dissent in the minutes.
A director interested in an item leaves the room. If the chairman is interested, another disinterested director takes the chair. Record this in the minutes.
Minutes show meeting number, date and time, venue, names of directors and invitees present and other details required by SS-1.
Send the draft to all directors, including those absent. Give them 7 days from circulation to comment.
Print, enter in the minutes book and have the chairman sign (physical books). If kept electronically, sign digitally to give a time stamp.
Send the signed minutes to all directors unless the board has waived this under SS-1.

checklist: Date within 120 days of last meeting
Agenda notes and draft resolutions sent
Minutes signed and entered in book
Signed minutes circulated or waiver taken

meetings.title: Board meeting (illustrative)
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

resolutions.title: Confirmation of minutes of previous meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the minutes of the meeting of the Board of Directors of {co} held on [date], as circulated to all directors, be and are hereby confirmed and signed by the Chairman.

resolutions.title: Date of next board meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the next meeting of the Board of Directors of {co} be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], which is within 120 days of this meeting as required by Section 173 of the Companies Act, 2013.

docs.title: Notice of board meeting
paras: NOTICE is given that meeting no. [number] of the Board of Directors of {co} will be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] [and by video conference / other audio-visual means, details: [link and instructions]] to transact the business in the attached agenda.
Draft notes to agenda and draft resolutions are enclosed. Directors wishing to join by video must tell the company secretary by [date]. By order of the Board. [Name], Company Secretary. Date: [date].

docs.title: Minutes of board meeting (outline)
paras: Minutes of meeting no. [number] of the Board of Directors of {co} held on [date], commencing at [time] and ending at [time], at [venue].

Present: [names of directors]. In attendance: [invitees]. Chairman: [name]. Quorum was present. Item 1: [matter]. After discussion it was RESOLVED THAT [text]. Directors who dissented: [names, or none]. Vote of thanks. Signed: [Chairman]. Date: [date]. Place: [place].

flags: The reference note says small private companies need 2 meetings in each half of the calendar year with a gap of at least 90 days. Section 173(5) as I know it requires one meeting in each half of the calendar year for small companies, one person companies and dormant companies, with a gap of at least 90 days. Verify.
The reference note does not state the number of meetings (at least four in a year, first within 30 days of incorporation) or the time limit to sign minutes under SS-1. Check.
The reference note limits the exemption to one person companies 'having only one director'. Check SS-1's exemption for OPCs.
private: Section 173, the Meetings of Board Rules and Secretarial Standard 1 apply to all companies except a One Person Company with only one director, so every step applies to a private company.

title: Holding a board meeting by video conference or audio-visual means
law: Section 173; Rules 3 and 4 of Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014; Secretarial Standard 1 and applicable MCA circulars
summary: How to hold a board meeting online, pass resolutions on screen and write the minutes so that they meet the Act and SS-1.
when: When directors cannot or do not wish to meet in person.
applies: All companies, subject to limits on matters that cannot be dealt with by video

steps.d: Prepare the notice and agenda for a meeting through video conference or other audio-visual means.
Create the meeting link and make sure the time slots on the platform are long enough.
Send the notice, agenda and working papers to directors, invitees and officers well within time.
At the meeting, make sure all invitees have joined. Elect the chairman if none is designated.

The chairman calls the roll. Each person states their name, where they are joining from, that they have the papers and that nobody else can access the meeting. An accompanying person may stay only with the chair's permission.
The chairman says the meeting is held by video under the Act, asks anyone who cannot see or hear properly to say so at once (the meeting is paused), and confirms quorum.

The coordinator shows the resolution. After discussion, the chairman asks for views for and against, gives his own view, and the votes are counted. An interested person leaves and rejoins only when the coordinator confirms. The chairman declares it passed (unanimously or by majority) or failed.
After all business, the chairman gives closing remarks and participants sign off.

In the heading, say the meeting was held by video conference or other audio-visual means, with the other SS-1 details. In the attendance, give each person's location and the items they took part in. Write in past tense, record the roll call, any technical disturbance and any disagreement, and follow all SS-1 requirements.

checklist: Notice states video conference mode and link
Interested directors' exit and return noted
Minutes show location of each participant

meetings.title: Board meeting by video conference
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

resolutions.title: Approval of video conference arrangements
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the Board meeting of {co} held on [date] through video conference or other audio-visual means under Section 173 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rules 3 and 4 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014 be recorded as duly held. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the platform [name of platform] used for the meeting be adopted for future meetings and [name of company secretary] be authorised to keep the attendance records and recordings of the meeting.

docs.title: Notice of board meeting by video conference
paras: NOTICE is given that meeting no. [number] of the Board of Directors of {co} will be held on [date] at [time] through video conference or other audio-visual means. Link: [link]. Meeting ID and password: [details].

Directors and invitees must join from a private place and must not share the link. The agenda and papers are enclosed. For technical help call [name and number]. By order of the Board. [Name], Company Secretary. Date: [date].

docs.title: Roll call and opening statement (script)
paras: Chairman: I confirm that this meeting is being held by video conference under Section 173 of the Companies Act, 2013 and SS-1. Please state your name, your location, that you have received the papers, and that no one else can access the meeting.
If you have difficulty seeing or hearing, tell me or the coordinator immediately and the meeting will pause. Quorum is present. We proceed to the agenda.

flags: The reference note does not give the notice period; Section 173(3) requires 7 days (shorter notice with consent) as for any board meeting.

The reference note does not mention the matters that Rule 4 does not allow to be dealt with by video (such as approval of annual financial statements and the board's report) or MCA relaxations over time. Check the current rule and circulars.
The reference note numbering is jumbled; I have used the logical order of the three parts (meeting, resolution, minutes).

title: Passing a board resolution by circulation
law: Section 175 read with Rule 5 of Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014
summary: Pass urgent board decisions between meetings by sending a draft to all directors and counting their written assent.
when: When a matter is urgent and does not have to be decided at a board meeting.
applies: All companies, private and public alike

steps.d: Send the draft with the necessary papers to all directors at their postal or email address registered with the company. Give each resolution a serial number.
Send by hand, speed post, registered post, courier, email or another recognised electronic mode.
For each item, give a note explaining its meaning, scope and effect.
Communicate any director's interest in the matter. If a director's interest has not yet been disclosed, the director must disclose it before the last date for response.
Say how to give assent or dissent and the last date for a reply. Give directors not more than 7 days, plus 2 more days if sent by speed post, registered post or courier.
steps.time: 7 days (+2 days for post or courier)

steps.d: The resolution passes if a majority of directors entitled to vote approve. If one-third or more of all directors ask for it to be decided at a meeting, put it before the next board meeting instead.

steps.t: Note it at the next board meeting
steps.d: The members present at the next board meeting note the resolution passed by circulation, and it goes into the minutes.
Keep proof of sending and confirmation of receipt. A director can ask for paper copies even if sent electronically.

checklist: Sent to all directors (including alternates and interested directors)
Proof of dispatch and receipt kept
Item is not on the list that needs a meeting

meetings.title: Resolution by circulation
meetings.notice_days: Response period: up to 7 days (+2 days for post or courier)

meetings.title: Next board meeting to note circular resolution
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if directors agree)

resolutions.title: Resolution passed by circulation
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 175 of the Companies Act, 2013, and Rule 5 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, approval of the Board of Directors of {co} be and is hereby given to [describe matter, with amount in Rs. if any]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director or company secretary] be authorised to take all steps needed to carry out this resolution.

resolutions.title: Noting the circular resolution
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the resolution no. [serial number] passed by circulation on [date] on [subject], approved by [number] of [total number] directors, be noted and recorded in the minutes of this meeting under Section 175 of the Companies Act, 2013.

docs.title: Covering note to directors
paras: To all Directors of {co}. Please find enclosed draft resolution no. [serial number] for approval by circulation, with an explanatory note and papers.

Directors interested in the matter must disclose their interest before [last date]. Please return the attached assent or dissent form by [last date, within 7 days; add 2 days for post or courier]. If one-third or more of the directors want the item decided at a meeting, it will go to the next board meeting. By order of the Board. [Name], Company Secretary. Date: [date].

docs.title: Assent or dissent form
paras: Resolution no. [serial number] of {co}. I, [name of director], [assent / dissent] to the resolution. Interest in the matter: [none / details]. Signed: [name]. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note says directors may be given 'not more than' 7 days to reply. I believe SS-1 and Rule 5 allow at least 7 days; the reference note reads like a limit rather than a minimum. Check Rule 5 and SS-1 clause on timing.

The reference note's long list of items that cannot be passed by circulation mixes legal items (Section 179(3) and Rule 8, such as calls, buy-back, issue of securities, borrowing, loans, financial statements, merger, takeover, KMP and internal or secretarial auditors) with SS-1 and listing-rule practice items. Check each against Rule 8 before treating it as barred by law.
The reference note says a majority approving is enough. Under Section 175 the majority is of directors entitled to vote, and the one-third rule applies; use the exact figures from the Act.
The reference note gives no rule for how an unresponsive director is counted; check SS-1.
private: A private company follows the same circulation procedure as a public company.

extras.h: Key points on a resolution by circulation
items: Use it for urgent matters that arise between Board meetings.
Send the draft with a note, the background and supporting papers to every director, including alternate directors and interested directors, at their registered addresses.
Send by hand, speed post, courier, e-mail or other recognised electronic means.
It is passed if a majority of the directors approve it.
If one-third or more of the directors ask for it to be decided at a meeting, put it to the next Board meeting.
Note it in the minutes of the next Board meeting.
Keep proof of sending and of receipt. A director may ask for the papers on paper even if they were sent electronically.

extras.h: Business that must not be passed by circulation (illustrative)
items: General: noting the minutes of the audit and other committees; approving the financial statements and Board's report; the compliance certificate and the list of applicable laws; appointing secretarial and internal auditors.

Specific: borrowing other than by debentures; investing the company's funds; loans, guarantees and security; political contributions; making calls on shares; remuneration of the Managing Director, whole-time director or manager; appointing or removing key managerial personnel; appointing a person as managing director or manager of more than one company; filling a casual vacancy among directors; related party transactions outside the ordinary course or not at arm's length; sale of subsidiaries; buying or selling material assets outside the ordinary course; payment to a director for loss of office; items arising from a separate meeting of independent directors.

Corporate actions: buy-back; issue of securities, including debentures, in or outside India; amalgamation, merger or reconstruction; diversifying the business; taking over or acquiring a controlling or substantial stake in another company.
A listed company has further items on the list, such as the annual operating plan and budgets.
